**- Anonymous post for someone else -**

We are a mixed Jewish and non-Jewish (Israeli-Canadian) couple, planning to get married civilly very soon and are living together in Canada. The jewish partner has an Israeli passport (but did not do Aliyah, and not planning to make one at this time), and the non-Jewish partner is currently in Israel on a tourist visa (waiting for an answer for the rabbanoute regarding her conversion process). 
We have a few questions about how to handle our situation:

If we get married civilly in Canada, when the Israeli partner returns to Israel this summer, to visit, should we inform the Ministry of Interior that we are then married?
The Jewish partner plans to come to Israel for approximately 6 months.

How should we proceed in this case? Will the Israeli partner be able to stay in Israel without any issues for those 6 months?

Any advice or experiences from people in similar situations would be greatly appreciated. 
Could the visa for the non jewish be switched while his husband to be is here?

Thank you!
